headline: Maui County Council Meeting

meeting.summary: The Council adopted a Pride Month resolution with nine ayes and zero noes and heard a request to buy land for a new upcountry well.
meeting.recap: The chair said the mayor signed the budget bill that morning.[[0:05:59]] Resolution 26-101 recognizes June 2026 as Pride Month in the County of Maui and honors Aloha Maui Pride.[[0:34:11]] A family services leader said Maui County lost two more preschools in the last month.[[1:03:03]] A testifier spoke in support of a housing project in Pāʻia town.[[1:08:16]] A testifier asked for a long-term lease so her group can care for burial sites in the Wailuku and Waikapū sand dunes.[[1:18:28]] A department representative asked the council to act today on Resolution 26-102, a land purchase for a new upcountry well.[[1:55:50]] He said the well would add one million gallons a day to the upcountry water system.[[1:57:01]] The chair asked him to come back when the item comes up.[[1:57:46]] The council postponed a proposed change to noise violation penalties until it takes up a related committee report.[[2:01:09]]
meeting.next: A council member asked for the department director or deputy to attend when the item is taken up, and a staff member said they could get them there.

issues.oneLine: The council heard a request to act today on buying land for a new upcountry well.
issues.why: The representative said the well, together with filter upgrades at a water treatment plant, would let the county resume processing the upcountry wait list.
issues.next: The chair asked the representative to come back when the item comes up.
issues.brief: The representative said the land price is $470,000.[[#1]] He said the purchase followed the standard process, including an independent appraisal (an outside estimate of the land's value).[[#2]] He said the well would add one million gallons a day to the upcountry system.[[#3]]

issues.oneLine: Testifiers spoke in support of a housing project in Pāʻia town.
issues.why: A testifier said many of his friends and classmates have been priced out and forced to move off the island.
issues.brief: A family services leader said working families cannot go to work without childcare and early education.[[#1]] Another testifier said Maui does not have enough housing to meet the needs of its residents.[[#2]]
